title: Paul Howard's Quality Serenaders and owner Frank Sebastian
summary: He names bandmates Paul Howard and George Orendorff, and describes Sebastian, who loved lights.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Did the entire house band at the Cotton Club work in the studios together then?

Yes, there was only eight men in the band at that time, so yes we were -- in fact the -- the -- what do you call the dance -- the person had the shows -- was Carolyn Snowden -- I think she's still alive. And this group called the Quality Serenaders was the band, or Paul Howard's Quality Serenaders it became.
And it was you, Paul Howard, and do you remember who else? Juff --
George Orendorff, Paul Howard, -- these names sort of escape me. You know how it is when you get old.
When and if they occur to you -- we'll drop them in when they occur to you. Paul Howard played what?

It was tenor saxophone. He's still alive. He's pretty old now but he's still here. In fact, there were so many things happened. We went in and out of that club and split up and went in together again, and different things you know. We --
What did Orendorff? Mr. Orendorff was playing what --
Arendoff was trumpet player. He finally wound up in the Postal Service, and I think now he is retired from the Postal Service. And --
The Cotton Club was run by Frank Sebastian.
Frank Sebastian, yes. The man that loved lights. He had lights all over the place. And neon lights and every light you could imagine. He was very -- well, he was a beautiful fellow. He was real fine.
